facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant took part in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
On 9 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 9 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having used violence against the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 9 June 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered the applicant's pre-trial detention until 9 August 2012.
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged under Articles 212 § 2 and 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riots, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 an investigation was launched into the criminal offence of organising acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it transpired that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, a police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
It took the police about two hours to clear the protestors from Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
According to the applicant, he was beaten up by the police as they were dispersing the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The examination at Sklifosovskiy hospital on 7 May 2012 revealed multiple bruises on the applicant's chest.
The examination at Sklifosovskiy hospital on 7 May 2012 revealed multiple bruises on the applicant's spine.
The examination at Sklifosovskiy hospital on 7 May 2012 revealed multiple bruises on the applicant's shoulders.
The examination at Sklifosovskiy hospital on 7 May 2012 revealed multiple bruises on the applicant's knees.
The examination at Sklifosovskiy hospital on 7 May 2012 revealed multiple bruises on the applicant's head.
The applicant was accused of having torn a protection helmet off a police officer's head during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had shouted insulting slogans during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had used metal barriers to obstruct the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had at least three times thrown stones and pieces of tarmac at police officers during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had once punched a policeman during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had grabbed a police officer's uniform during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had snatched a protection helmet from a police officer's hands during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 29 November 2012 Police Officer P. identified the applicant during an identification parade as a participant in the mass disorder at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

On 29 November 2012 Police Officer P. identified the applicant during an identification parade as the person who had twice thrown pieces of tarmac at the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

On 29 November 2012 Police Officer P. identified the applicant during an identification parade as the person who had tried to snatch a protection helmet from a policeman's hands during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
Police Officer P. specified during the identification parade on 29 November 2012 that he had not seen whether the applicant had in fact succeeded in snatching the helmet or not.

On 7 December 2012 the investigator of the Zamoskvoretskiy Inter-district Investigation Committee of Moscow refused to open a criminal case into allegations made by the applicant that he had been subjected to ill-treatment by the police during his arrest.

The investigator of the Zamoskvoretskiy Inter-district Investigation Committee of Moscow considered on 7 December 2012 that the use of force by the police had been justified by the behaviour of the protesters, including the applicant, who had actively resisted their arrest.

The investigator of the Zamoskvoretskiy Inter-district Investigation Committee of Moscow considered on 7 December 2012 that the use of force by the police had been justified by the behaviour of the protesters, including the applicant, who had thrown various objects at the police officers.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue and to defy the lawful orders of the police.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that unidentified persons called those present at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials in connection with the performance of their duties and the destruction of property.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that on 6 May 2012 at 5 p.m. at the latest the defendants acquired the criminal intent to participate in mass disorder and to use violence against police officers.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that participants of the acts of mass disorder threw pieces of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, which hit them on various parts of their body.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that between 5.05 p.m. and 10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the applicant shouted insulting slogans and used metal barriers to block the police's movement, thus preventing the arrest of the participants in the acts of mass disorder.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant, acting intentionally, at least three times threw stones and pieces of tarmac at police officers in a targeted manner during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant used violence against an unidentified police officer which did not endanger his life or health during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that unidentified participants in the acts of mass disorder tore a protection helmet off an unidentified police officer's head and punched and kicked him several times in the head and body, while the applicant punched this police officer at least once.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant used violence against Police Officer T. which did not endanger his life or health during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that unidentified participants of the acts of mass disorder intentionally tore off Police Officer T.'s protection helmet, which T. continued to hold in his hands, and punched him in the head and body, whereupon the applicant intentionally grabbed T.'s uniform and snatched the helmet from his hands.
The applicant pleaded not guilty at his criminal trial before the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.
The applicant testified at his criminal trial that he had decided to attend the public gathering on 6 May 2012.

The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when leaving the Malyy Kamennyy Bridge he saw a lot of police officers equipped with bullet-proof vests, helmets and truncheons, which filled him with indignation.

The applicant testified at his criminal trial that as nothing was happening on the stage, he decided to return, and when leaving the venue he saw the police officers randomly arresting people while hitting them with truncheons.
The applicant testified at his criminal trial that he was hit in the back three times with a truncheon.
The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when he saw violent acts by the police, he approached the barriers where other protestors were standing and expressed his indignation.
The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when trying to leave the venue, somebody tore off his shirt.
The applicant testified at his criminal trial that at some point he came across Police Officer T., who was not wearing any helmet.

The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when he tried to leave, police officers ran up to him and started to beat him in the head and body, then arrested him and took him to a police vehicle.
The applicant insisted at his criminal trial that he had committed no acts in respect of Police Officer T., had not seen his helmet and had snatched nothing from his hands.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow considered the defendants' arguments that they were protecting somebody from police officers or happened to be victims of the police's use of force as farfetched and aimed at mitigating their responsibility.

In his appeal, the applicant complained that he had not used metal barriers to block the police's movement and insisted that he had been standing close to those barriers before the protestors had started to be arrested.
In his appeal, the applicant pointed out that the video records proved that he had not taken Police Officer T.'s helmet and had not used violence against him.
In his appeal, the applicant argued that the first-instance court had not assessed his statements about ill-treatment by the police.
On 20 June 2014 the Moscow City Court upheld the first-instance judgment of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow of 21 February 2014.
